title: I had plans for that second
description: Two unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities, collectively dubbed 'php2shell', affect PHP versions since 5.4. These flaws can be triggered by a simple HTTP request and pose a critical risk to all industries running PHP applications, including popular platforms like WordPress and Drupal. Older PHP branches are end-of-life and will not receive patches, representing about half of use cases. Cisco Talos has released Snort signatures to detect exploitation attempts. Immediate upgrading to PHP 8.2 or later is strongly advised, as no patches exist for PHP 8.1 or earlier.
aiSummary: Two critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities were discovered in PHP, affecting all builds since version 5.4. These vulnerabilities, known as 'php2shell', can be triggered by a simple HTTP request, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code remotely. Given PHP's widespread use in major web platforms such as WordPress, Drupal, Magento, Shopware, and WooCommerce, the potential impact is extensive. Older PHP branches are no longer supported and will not receive patches, which could account for approximately 50% of deployments. Cisco Talos has published Snort intrusion detection rules (IDs 67359 and 67360) to help detect exploitation attempts. The recommended mitigation is immediate upgrade to PHP 8.2 or later, as no patches are available for PHP 8.1 or earlier versions.
aiImpact: Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities allows unauthenticated remote code execution on affected PHP servers, potentially leading to full system compromise. The widespread use of PHP in popular content management and e-commerce platforms increases the blast radius significantly. Systems running unsupported PHP versions remain vulnerable without available patches, increasing risk exposure.
